The Pool barb Puntius sophore is a small cyprinid widely distributed across South and Southeast Asia, where it inhabits ponds, ditches, and slow-flowing streams. Field surveys indicate that females attain sexual maturity at 5 cm [Lp = 5 cm] in total length, a relatively modest size that reflects the species' opportunistic life-history strategy in seasonally fluctuating environments. In laboratory rearing trials conducted at 22 °C [T = 22 °C], the maximum recorded reproductive output reached approximately 63 eggs per day per female [Ri = approximately 63 eggs per day per female] when conditions of abundant food and stable water quality were maintained, a level of fecundity that positions this species among the more prolific members of the genus. Hatchlings emerge from demersal, adhesive eggs at a wet weight of only 0.0026 grams [Wwb = 0.0026 grams], a mass consistent with the small egg diameters typical of cyprinids that broadcast spawn over submerged vegetation. The larvae are initially endotrophic, subsisting on endogenous yolk reserves for several days before the onset of exogenous feeding, at which point they begin to forage on rotifers and small cladocerans.

As adults, Puntius sophore exhibit a maximum recorded total length of 20 centimeters [Li = 20 centimeters] under optimal conditions, although most individuals in natural populations rarely exceed 16 centimeters due to ecological constraints such as predation pressure and seasonal resource limitation. The corresponding asymptotic body mass derived from length-weight relationships indicates an ultimate wet weight of about 97 grams [Wwi = about 97 grams] for the largest individuals, a value that underscores the species' relatively modest body size compared to other cyprinids of similar habitat preferences. Growth rates are strongly influenced by water temperature, with the highest somatic growth observed during the monsoon months when both thermal conditions and food availability peak. Comparative data from related species suggest that this growth trajectory is typical of short-lived, iteroparous cyprinids that allocate a substantial proportion of their energy budget toward reproductive effort rather than continued somatic expansion later in life. Juveniles recruit into the breeding population within their first year, a rapid maturation schedule that compensates for relatively high natural mortality rates in the early life stages.

At the population level, the reproductive strategy of Puntius sophore is characterized by a high daily fecundity rate that is tightly coupled to the warm, productive conditions of the wet season. Gravid females collected from floodplain habitats during the peak spawning period produce clutches averaging 1,500 to 2,000 eggs per spawning event [N_R_i = 1,500 to 2,000 eggs per spawning event], with individual females capable of completing approximately 1.6 such events per week [F_R_i = approximately 1.6 such events per week] when water temperatures remain near 22 °C [T = 22 °C]. This translates into a substantial cumulative reproductive output over the course of a single breeding season, a pattern that is energetically demanding and likely contributes to the relatively short life span observed in the species. Egg diameter measurements from preserved specimens average 1.7 millimeters, a size that is consistent with the calculated wet weight at birth derived from geometric formulas. The fertilized ova are demersal and adhesive, attaching to submerged aquatic plants and roots, a spawning behavior that reduces egg predation by benthic foragers.

The maximum longevity of Puntius sophore in its natural environment is approximately 6 years [am = approximately 6 years], a lifespan that is relatively brief when compared to larger cyprinids like the common carp or mahseer species, a pattern consistent with the negative correlation between body size and mortality rate that prevails across teleost fishes at a temperature of 22 °C [T = 22 °C]. This estimate is based on mark-recapture studies conducted in perennial ponds where water temperatures consistently average 22 °C [T = 22 °C]. Field observations indicate that senescent individuals exhibit a gradual decline in condition factor, reduced gonadosomatic indices, and increased susceptibility to ectoparasitic infections during their final year. The trade-off between high reproductive investment early in life and reduced survival later is a classic life-history syndrome observed in many tropical freshwater fishes that occupy unpredictable environments. Captive individuals maintained under optimal conditions have been documented to survive slightly beyond this age, suggesting that the wild lifespan is constrained primarily by extrinsic mortality factors such as predation and seasonal desiccation rather than by an intrinsic physiological limit.

Ecologically, Puntius sophore plays an important role as both a consumer of zooplankton and detritus and as a forage fish for piscivorous birds and larger predatory fishes. The species exhibits a wide thermal tolerance, surviving in waters ranging from 14 °C to 34 °C, although reproductive activity is largely confined to the warmer months when temperatures exceed 20 °C. Comparative studies with the congener Puntius ticto have revealed subtle differences in spawning phenology, with P. sophore initiating breeding slightly earlier in the monsoon season, a divergence that may reduce interspecific competition for spawning substrates. The species is also known to undertake short-distance lateral migrations onto inundated floodplains during the rainy season, exploiting the temporary abundance of food resources and the reduced predation risk in these shallow, turbid waters. Juvenile growth during these floodplain phases is remarkably rapid, with young-of-the-year reaching lengths of 4 to 6 centimeters by the onset of the dry season, enabling them to achieve sexual maturity and contribute to the next generation before the habitat contracts. This opportunistic life-history template has made Puntius sophore a resilient inhabitant of anthropogenically modified wetlands across its extensive range.
